bugs: Array-valued email (email[]=x) causes 500 instead of 422: limiter key in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25-27 casts input via str() before validation runs
Throttle key lowercases email but lookup at app/Http/Controllers/Auth/TokenController.php:17 is case-sensitive, so 'J@E.COM' gets 401 for a valid user (inconsistent normalisation)
Requests missing email all share the '|ip' bucket (minor)
antipatterns: app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:26 ->trim() is redundant: global TrimStrings middleware already trims input
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:175 pointless Hash::check assertion on the factory password in the end-to-end test
strengths: Authenticated routes grouped under one auth:sanctum middleware group (routes/api.php)
Named RateLimiter keyed by email+IP and applied via throttle middleware
Uses currentAccessToken()->delete() and only() for a minimal /me body
Tests use describe blocks, check truly missing fields with except(), assert exact validation messages, check that other tokens survive revocation, and check that the window resets with travel()

bugs: Array-valued email causes 500 instead of 422: limiter key in app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25-26 casts input via str() before validation runs
Throttle key lowercases email but lookup at app/Http/Controllers/Auth/TokenController.php:17 is case-sensitive, so a differently cased valid email gets 401
Requests missing email all share the '|ip' bucket (minor)
antipatterns: routes/api.php:13-14 repeats ->middleware('auth:sanctum') per route instead of a group
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:24-25 separate expect() calls instead of chaining with ->and(); assertion message check at :38 is loose (substring of field name)
tests/Feature/TokenAuthTest.php:36 sends null rather than omitting the field (still covers 'required')
strengths: Same lean controller/FormRequest/named-limiter design with no extra ceremony
Tests show a correct password is still blocked once throttled, and that the window reset works
Tests cover non-JSON clients getting 401 (get/delete without Accept JSON), plus an empty body
Uses assertTooManyRequests(), and checks that only the current token is revoked by plucking names

v.rationale: Both implementations are nearly identical in production code and behave the same in every probe. They share the same small bugs: an array-valued email gives 500 because the limiter runs before validation, and the email casing used in the throttle key does not match the case-sensitive user lookup. impl-1 groups the authenticated routes more cleanly but adds a redundant trim(). impl-2 has slightly stronger focus-area tests: a correct password still gets 429 when throttled, non-JSON clients get 401, an empty body is covered, and it uses assertTooManyRequests(). impl-1's tests have a pointless Hash::check line and use assertStatus(429). It is a narrow edge to impl-2.
